title: Rubix as a Net-Zero Blockchain
content: Rubix can be positioned as a net-zero blockchain by eliminating energy-intensive mining and avoiding global block competition. Its architecture enables significantly lower energy consumption per transaction compared to traditional proof-of-work systems, making it suitable for sustainable digital infrastructure.

title: No Proof-of-Work Mining
content: Unlike Bitcoin, Rubix does not rely on proof-of-work mining, which consumes large amounts of electricity. Instead, it uses a pledge-based validation model, drastically reducing computational overhead and carbon emissions.

title: Parallel Tokenchain Architecture Reduces Waste
content: Rubix processes transactions in parallel across tokenchains rather than forcing all transactions into a single global chain. This avoids redundant computation across the network, reducing energy waste and improving efficiency.

title: No Global Mempool or Fee Auction
content: Rubix avoids global mempool competition and gas fee auctions, which often lead to excessive computation and energy waste in other blockchains. This contributes to a lower overall environmental footprint.

title: Reuse of Existing Infrastructure
content: Rubix allows enterprises to reuse existing infrastructure as nodes instead of requiring specialized mining hardware. This reduces capital expenditure and avoids additional environmental impact from new hardware production.

title: Low Energy Per Transaction
content: Because Rubix does not rely on global consensus for every transaction, each transaction consumes significantly less energy. This makes Rubix suitable for high-frequency enterprise use cases without increasing carbon footprint.

title: Carbon Accounting and Offsetting Support
content: Rubix can support carbon accounting by tracking emissions data on-chain and enabling tokenization of carbon credits. Organizations can build verifiable net-zero workflows directly on the network.

title: Net-Zero Positioning Narrative
content: Rubix should be positioned as a net-zero digital infrastructure layer: low energy consumption, no mining, efficient parallel processing, and support for carbon tracking and offsets. This makes it aligned with ESG goals and climate-conscious enterprise adoption.
